test: step corrections survive reload and undo launches the requested redo with visible history
expected: the Jevellan web app "undo retry" screen at desktop-light, rendered completely and legibly (one of several screens captured during "step corrections survive reload and undo launches the requested redo with visible history"; the other steps are judged in their own screenshots)

cosmetic: The error text repeats 'disabled' six times ('disabled, disabled, disabled, disabled, disabled, disabled'), which reads like a raw list of model states rather than a clear user-facing message.
The same 'No model can run this step right now' message shows twice: once in the red banner and again in the 'Resume correction · step 1' card.

Conversation titles and subtitles in the sidebar are cut off with ellipses (e.g. 'Change the value to thre…', 'Context · J11 memory journ…'). This is intentional overflow handling, and the full title is visible in the header.
The correction tags in the step header ('corrected: effort → max', 'corrected: action → reply, effort → low') are small, low-contrast pink text and somewhat hard to read.
The 'Step 1 · Implement' title is struck through and greyed out to show it was undone. This is intentional but reduces contrast.
